trip.name: Olympic Peninsula Adventure
trip.summary: A three-day scenic road trip through the Olympic Peninsula, exploring lakes, rain forests, and rugged coastline.

coverImage.altText: Lake and mountains in Olympic National Park

dogFriendly.details: Dog access varies by destination. Many developed areas allow leashed dogs.

kidFriendly.details: Includes short, flexible scenic stops suitable for all ages.

olderAdultFriendly.details: Some areas require trail walking; scenic overlooks are easier.

wheelchairAccessible.details: Accessibility varies by stop. Developed areas are generally accessible.

strollerFriendly.details: Best near lodges and developed viewpoints.

days.title: Port Angeles to Lake Crescent
days.summary: Begin at the waterfront and continue west to the stunning glacial lake.

stops.name: Port Angeles Waterfront
stops.summary: A relaxed waterfront start to the trip.
stops.description: Pick up supplies, grab coffee, and enjoy a short walk along the harbor.
stops.history: Port Angeles has served as the gateway to the Olympic Peninsula since the 1800s.

dogFriendly.details: Leashed dogs welcome on the waterfront.

kidFriendly.details: Easy flat walking with open views.

wheelchairAccessible.details: Most of the waterfront path is paved.

travelerTips.text: Download anything you need before entering lower-service areas west of here.

stops.name: Lake Crescent
stops.summary: A deep glacial lake with stunning clarity and mountain views.
stops.description: Enjoy the lodge area, walk the shoreline, and take in the deep blue water surrounded by forested mountains.
stops.history: Lake Crescent was formed by glaciers thousands of years ago and later separated from the Elwha River system.

mapReference.formattedAddress: Lake Crescent, Olympic National Park, WA

heroImage.altText: Clear blue water at Lake Crescent

dogFriendly.details: Developed areas may allow leashed dogs; many trails do not.

kidFriendly.details: Easy to enjoy near the lodge area.

olderAdultFriendly.details: Scenic views with limited walking required.

reviews.title: Beautiful in the morning
reviews.text: Early arrival made parking easier and the reflections were gorgeous.

travelerTips.text: Check trail-specific dog restrictions before leaving the developed area.

routeHighlights.name: Madison Falls
routeHighlights.description: A short, easy waterfall stop just off the highway.

days.title: Hoh Rain Forest & Sol Duc
days.summary: Explore one of the largest temperate rain forests in the US and a spectacular waterfall.

stops.name: Hoh Rain Forest
stops.summary: Walk through towering moss-covered trees in a temperate rain forest.
stops.description: The Hoh Rain Forest is one of the finest examples of a temperate rain forest in the United States. Expect lush green canopies, moss-draped branches, and serene forest sounds.
stops.history: The Hoh River Valley receives over 12 feet of rain annually, creating one of the most unique ecosystems in North America.

mapReference.formattedAddress: Hoh Rain Forest, Olympic National Park, WA

heroImage.altText: Moss-covered trees in Hoh Rain Forest

mustDo: Walk the Hall of Mosses trail

dogFriendly.details: Dogs are not permitted on Hoh Rain Forest trails.

kidFriendly.details: Hall of Mosses is a short, flat loop.

olderAdultFriendly.details: Hall of Mosses is manageable; longer trails are more demanding.

wheelchairAccessible.details: The mini trail near the Visitor Center is accessible.

strollerFriendly.details: Possible on the paved mini trail only.

reviews.title: Magical forest
reviews.text: Feels like stepping into another world. The moss everywhere is incredible.

travelerTips.text: Dogs are NOT allowed on trails here. Plan for someone to stay with pets or skip this stop.

stops.name: Sol Duc Falls
stops.summary: A beautiful waterfall at the end of a forested trail.
stops.description: Sol Duc Falls is reached via a 0.8-mile trail through old-growth forest. The waterfall splits into three channels over a rocky ledge.
stops.history: Sol Duc means 'sparkling water' in the Quileute language.

mapReference.formattedAddress: Sol Duc Falls Trail, Olympic National Park, WA

heroImage.altText: Sol Duc Falls cascading over mossy rocks

dogFriendly.details: Dogs are not permitted on this trail.

kidFriendly.details: Short trail suitable for children who can walk 1.6 miles round trip.

olderAdultFriendly.details: Mostly flat with some uneven sections and tree roots.

strollerFriendly.details: Unpaved trail with roots and uneven terrain.

travelerTips.text: Go early or late to avoid the midday crowds at the falls.

routeHighlights.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort
routeHighlights.description: Natural mineral hot springs with developed soaking pools.

mapReference.formattedAddress: Sol Duc Hot Springs Road, WA

image.altText: Hot springs pools surrounded by forest

olderAdultFriendly.details: Warm soaking pools with easy access.

days.title: Ruby Beach & Coastal Drive
days.summary: Experience the dramatic Pacific coastline with sea stacks, driftwood, and tide pools.

stops.name: Ruby Beach
stops.summary: A dramatic stretch of coastline with sea stacks and driftwood.
stops.description: Ruby Beach features iconic sea stacks rising from the surf, massive driftwood logs, and tide pools teeming with life. The beach is accessed via a short trail from the parking area.
stops.history: Named for the reddish-colored crystals sometimes found in the sand, Ruby Beach is one of the most photographed beaches on the Olympic coast.

mapReference.formattedAddress: Ruby Beach, Olympic National Park, WA

heroImage.altText: Sea stacks at Ruby Beach during golden hour

mustDo: Explore tide pools at low tide

dogFriendly.details: Dogs allowed on leash on Olympic coast beaches.

kidFriendly.details: Kids love the tide pools and driftwood climbing.

olderAdultFriendly.details: The trail to the beach is short but steep with uneven steps.

wheelchairAccessible.details: Trail to beach is steep and sandy.

strollerFriendly.details: Sandy trail not suitable for strollers.

reviews.title: Best beach on the peninsula
reviews.text: Came for sunset and it was absolutely worth it. The sea stacks create incredible compositions.

travelerTips.text: Ferro loved this beach! Keep dogs on leash and watch for sneaker waves.

stops.name: Kalaloch Beach & Tree of Life
stops.summary: Visit the famous tree clinging to an eroding cliff.
stops.description: The Tree of Life (Tree Root Cave) is a Sitka spruce that has survived despite the cliff beneath it eroding away, leaving its roots dramatically exposed.
stops.history: The tree has become one of the most photographed natural features on the Olympic coast.

mapReference.formattedAddress: Kalaloch Beach, Olympic National Park, WA

heroImage.altText: Tree of Life with exposed roots over eroded cliff

dogFriendly.details: Dogs allowed on leash on the beach.

kidFriendly.details: Short walk to an amazing natural feature.

olderAdultFriendly.details: Short walk from parking but terrain can be uneven.

travelerTips.text: Quick stop—15 minutes is enough to see the tree and snap photos.

routeHighlights.name: Beach 4 Tide Pools
routeHighlights.description: Excellent tide pools accessible at low tide, with sea stars and anemones.

olderAdultFriendly.details: Rocky, uneven terrain near tide pools.
